evidence.summary: Probe t7 compared group_quant_dequant against a per-group reference that handles a shorter trailing group. For n_cols=100 (36 tail cols), 65 (1 tail col) and 200 (8 tail cols) with group_size=64, every tail column of the kernel output is exactly 0 while the reference tail has nonzero magnitudes (max |ref| = 3.1298, 0.8738, 1.3475 respectively), giving max abs errors equal to those magnitudes. Columns inside complete groups match bit-exactly (head_max_abs_err = 0.0), and n_cols=64/128 match exactly. This is exactly the truncation of n_groups = n_cols // GROUP leaving zeros_like output untouched.

rationale: Line 12 computes n_groups by integer division and the loop at line 14 only covers full groups; out is initialized with torch.zeros_like, so tail columns are never written.

scope_evidence.summary: Input domain paragraph requires handling n_cols not a multiple of group_size, with the trailing shorter group getting its own scale.
'Every column of the input must be quantized under the scale of the group it belongs to.'

scope_rationale: problem.txt explicitly declares the input domain: n_cols may be any positive integer, is NOT required to be a multiple of group_size, and the trailing columns "form a shorter final group, which is still a group with its own scale". A representative admitted input is n_cols=100 with group_size=64.
statement: When n_cols is not a multiple of group_size, group_quant_dequant leaves the trailing partial-group columns as zeros instead of quantizing them under their own group scale (loop bound n_groups = n_cols // GROUP truncates).

evidence.summary: kernel.py line 20 uses tl.floor(x / scale + 0.5), i.e. round-half-up, whereas torch.round is round-half-to-even. problem.txt only says "round(x / scale)" without specifying a tie-break rule, and exact half-way quotients are measure-zero on the randn-style inputs the contract admits; probe t7 showed head (complete-group) columns matching torch.round bit-exactly (max abs err 0.0) across n_cols in {64,65,100,128,200}, so no rounding divergence was observed in practice. Not decisive either way.

rationale: Line 20 uses floor(x/s+0.5), which is round-half-up rather than round-half-away-from-zero or banker's rounding.
scope_rationale: problem.txt says 'round' without specifying tie-break; exact half-way values are measure-zero on typical float inputs, so this may be an unspecified detail.
statement: Rounding via tl.floor(x/scale + 0.5) differs from the contract's round() for negative half-way values (rounds -0.5 to 0 instead of away from zero / to even), causing per-element mismatch.
